The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+C) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(2(x+\frac{C}{2}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{C}{2}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2(x+\frac{C}{2}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14260558/assets/cac3ea6b8409290b6716a194325a885672e06572c1f8a8b63b48b6807f514d42.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)$ by $\frac{\pi }{12}$ units to the left. Therefore

$$
\frac{C}{2}=\frac{\pi }{12}\,⟹\,C=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$
